text: If the matrix $A=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 0 & 2 \\ K & -1 \end{array}\right )$ satisfies $A(A^{3}+3I)=2I$, then the value of K is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given matrix $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & 2 \\ k & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{4}+3IA=2I$

$\Rightarrow A^{4}=2I-3A$

Also characteristic equation of A is $|A-λI|=0$

$\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{ll} 0-λ & 2 \\ k & -1-λ \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow λ+λ^{2}-2k=0$

$\Rightarrow A+A^{2}=2K.I$

$\Rightarrow A^{2}=2KI-A$

$\Rightarrow A^{4}=4K^{2}I+A^{2}-4AK$

Put $A^{2}=2KI-A$

and $A^{4}=2I-3A$

$2I-3A=4K^{2}I+2KI-A-4AK$

$\Rightarrow I(2-2K-4K^{2})=A(2-4K)$

$\Rightarrow -2I(2K^{2}+K-1)=2A(1-2K)$

$\Rightarrow -2I(2K-1)(K+1)=2A(1-2K)$

$\Rightarrow (2K-1)(2A)-2I(2K-1)(K+1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (2K-1)[2A-2I(K+1)]=0$

$\Rightarrow K=\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation

 $\frac{dy}{dx}=2(y+2\sin x-5)x-2\cos x$ such that y(0) = 7. Then y($π$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy=2(2\sin x-5)x-2\cos x$

IF = $e^{-x^{2}}$

So, $y.e^{-x^{2}}=\int e^{-x^{2}}(2x(2\sin x-5)-2\cos x)dx$

$\Rightarrow y.e^{-x^{2}}=e^{-x^{2}}(5-2\sin x)+c$

$\Rightarrow y=5-2\sin x+c.e^{x^{2}}$

Given at x = 0, y = 7

$\Rightarrow$ 7 = 5 + c $\Rightarrow$ c = 2

So, $y=5-2\sin x+2e^{x^{2}}$

Now, at x = $π$,

y = 5 + 2$e^{π^{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: Let us consider a curve, y = f(x) passing through the point ($-$2, 2) and the slope of the tangent to the curve at any point (x, f(x)) is given by $f(x) + xf'(x) = x^{2}$. Then :

solution.body:
$y+\frac{xdy}{dx}=x^{2}$ (given)

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=x$

If $e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx}=x$

Solution of DE

$\Rightarrow xy=\frac{x^{3}}{3}+\frac{c}{3}$

Passes through ($-$2, 2), so

$-$12 = $-$ 8 + c $\Rightarrow$ c = $-$ 4

$\therefore$ $3xy = x^{3}$ $-$ 4

$i.e. 3x . f(x) = x^{3}$ $-$ 4

text: When a certain biased die is rolled, a particular face occurs with probability $\frac{1}{6}-x$ and its opposite face occurs with probability $\frac{1}{6}+x$. All other faces occur with probability $\frac{1}{6}$. Note that opposite faces sum to 7 in any die. If 0 < x < $\frac{1}{6}$, and the probability of obtaining total sum = 7, when such a die is rolled twice, is $\frac{13}{96}$, then the value of x is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Probability of obtaining total sum 7 = probability of getting opposite faces.

Probability of getting opposite faces

$=2\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}-x\right )\left (\frac{1}{6}+x\right )+\frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{6}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow 2\left [\left (\frac{1}{6}-x\right )\left (\frac{1}{6}+x\right )+\frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{6}\right ]=\frac{13}{96}$ (given)

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\frac{1}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: If $x^{2} + 9y^{2}$ $-$ 4x + 3 = 0, x, y $\in$ R, then x and y respectively lie in the intervals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2} + 9y^{2}$ $-$ 4x + 3 = 0

$(x^{2}$ $-$ $4x) + (9y^{2}) + 3 = 0$

$(x^{2}$ $-$ $4x + 4) + (9y^{2}) + 3$ $-$ 4 = 0

(x $-$ $2)^{2} + (3y)^{2} = 1$

$\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{(1)^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{\left (\frac{1}{3}\right )^{2}}=1$ (equation of an ellipse).

As it is equation of an ellipse, x & y can vary inside the ellipse.

So, $x-2\in [-1,1]$ and $y\in \left [-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right ]$

x $\in$ [1, 3] $y\in \left [-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}\right ]$

text: A wire of length 20 m is to be cut into two pieces. One of the pieces is to be made into a square and the other into a regular hexagon. Then the length of the side (in meters) of the hexagon, so that the combined area of the square and the hexagon is minimum, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the wire is cut into two pieces of length x and 20 $-$ x.


[IMG]


Area of square = $\left (\frac{x}{4}\right )^{2}$ 

Area of regular hexagon = $6\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\left (\frac{20-x}{6}\right )^{2}$

Total area = $A(x)=\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\frac{(20-x)^{2}}{36}$

$A^{'}(x)=\frac{2x}{16}+\frac{3\sqrt{3}\times 2}{2\times 36}(20-x)(-1)$

A'(x) = 0 at $x=\frac{40\sqrt{3}}{3+2\sqrt{3}}$

Length of side of regular Hexagon $=\frac{1}{6}(20-x)$

$=\frac{1}{6}\left (20-\frac{40\sqrt{3}}{3+2\sqrt{3}}\right )$

$=\frac{10}{3+2\sqrt{3}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

solution.body:

B = ($-\infty$, $-$2) $\cup$ (2, $\infty$)

C = ($-\infty$, 2] $\cup$ [6, $\infty$)

z $\cap$ (A $\cap$ B $\cap$ C)' = {$-$2, $-$1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

Hence, no. of its subsets $= 2^{8} = 256$.

text:
If the system of linear equations

2x + y $-$ z = 3

x $-$ y $-$ z = $α$

3x + 3y + $β$z = 3

has infinitely many solutions, then $α$ + $β$ $-$ $αβ$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2 $\times$ (i) $-$ (ii) $-$ (iii) gives :

$-$ (1 + $β$)z = 3 $-$ $α$

For infinitely many solution

$β$ + 1 = 0 = 3 $-$ $α$ $\Rightarrow$ ($α$, $β$) = (3, $-$1)

Hence, $α$ + $β$ $-$ $αβ$ = 5

text: A number is called a palindrome if it reads the same backward as well as forward. For example 285582 is a six digit palindrome. The number of six digit palindromes, which are divisible by 55, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
5
    a
    b
    b
    a
    5
  

For divisible by 55 it shall be divisible by 11 and 5
both, for divisibility by 5 unit digit shall be 0 or 5 but
as the number is six digit palindrome unit digit is 5.

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between sum of the digits in the odd places and the sum of the digits in the even places is a multiple of 11 or zero.

Sum of the digits in the even place = a + b + 5

Sum of the digits in the odd places = a + b + 5

Difference between the two sums = (a + b + 5 ) - (a + b + 5) = 0

0 is divisible by 11.

Hence, 5abba5 is divisible by 11.

So, required number = 10 $\times$ 10 = 100
